h1: The 7 Best Roborock Robot Vacuums of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Roborock Robot Vacuums 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: seven Roborock robot vacuums from Saros flagship to Q7 entry, sorted by suction, mopping, docks and who each one suits.
summary: The Roborock Saros 10R is the best Roborock for buyers who want the complete package: 22000Pa suction, LiDAR navigation and an edge arm for corners. The Qrevo S Pro gets close at 18,500Pa for less. The Qrevo S5V adds FlexiArm edge mopping under $500, and the Q7 M5+ suits busy homes with its long self-empty interval.
intro: Roborock names do not tell you what you are giving up as you move down the range. A Saros, a Qrevo and a Q series model can all clean a floor, yet the real differences sit in places the spec headline skips: how the dock handles dust and water, and whether the robot has any hardware to reach the corners a round body cannot. That is where buyers overspend or come up short.

We ranked seven Roborock models from their listings, scoring stated suction, navigation, mopping and dock behavior on the Primea framework. Treat the price brackets as an indicator of tier rather than a quote, because dock bundles and sales change what you actually pay at checkout. Suction headlines get the attention, but we weighted dock automation and edge coverage at least as heavily, since those decide how often you touch the machine.

products.name: roborock Saros 10R Robot Vacuum and Mop, 22000Pa, Edge Cleaning
products.verdict: Flagship suction with an arm that reaches edges and corners.
products.description:
The Saros 10R is Roborock's flagship, and the numbers show it. It lists 22000Pa suction, LiDAR navigation, vacuum plus mop in one chassis and an edge cleaning arm that reaches into corners and along baseboards. Round robots leave crescents of dust in square corners, which is a real daily irritation, and the arm exists specifically to close that gap.

It ranks first because it combines the top suction in this ranking with the most thorough edge coverage. Against the Qrevo S Pro, you gain 3,500Pa and the arm, but you pay the top $500+ price. The Q7 M5+ costs far less, yet its 10000Pa is less than half the Saros.

Buy it if budget is not the constraint and you want the most complete clean. Skip it for a small apartment: the price and the power are both more than you need.
products.idealFor: Buyers wanting the most complete edge and corner cleaning.
products.skipIf: You are on a tight budget.

products.name: roborock 2026 New Qrevo S Pro Robot Vacuum and Mop, 18,500Pa Suction
products.verdict: Near-flagship 18,500Pa suction with premium dock features.
products.description:
Roborock's 2026 Qrevo S Pro is the flagship for people who do not need the flagship price. It lists 18,500Pa suction, LiDAR mapping and premium dock features, and it still sits in the $500+ bucket. The suction figure alone puts it well above the 10000Pa Q-series pair and close to the Saros.

It ranks second because it gives up the Saros edge arm and 3,500Pa, but keeps the parts most owners notice daily: strong suction and a capable dock. It also edges past the plain Qrevo Series, which lists no suction figure at all, so you cannot verify what you are buying there.

Buy it if you want near-flagship cleaning without Saros pricing. Skip it if square corners bother you, because no edge arm is listed. It also remains a $500+ machine, so the saving over the Saros is partial, not dramatic.
products.idealFor: Buyers wanting strong suction and dock features for less.
products.skipIf: You want the edge cleaning arm.

products.name: roborock Qrevo Series Robot Vacuum and Mop, Upgraded from Qrevo S
products.verdict: Mop lifting and an auto-empty dock for hard floors plus carpet.
products.description:
The Qrevo Series is the pick for homes that mix hard floor and carpet. It is an upgrade over the Qrevo S, and it lists LiDAR navigation, an auto-empty dock and mop lifting. Lifting the mop matters because a wet pad dragged across a rug leaves it damp and smelling, so the robot raises it as it crosses onto carpet.

It lands third because the listing states no suction figure, while the Qrevo S Pro behind it publishes 18,500Pa. Without a number, you are buying on features alone. Its mop lifting is the argument against the cheaper Qrevo S5V, which keeps edge mopping but no lifting claim.

Buy it if you have rugs on hard floors and want a self-emptying dock. Skip it if you rank suction on paper first. It also sits in the $500+ bracket, so you pay flagship prices for a model with fewer published specs.
products.idealFor: Homes with mixed hard floors and carpet.
products.skipIf: You want a published suction number.

products.name: roborock Qrevo S5V Robot Vacuum and Mop, FlexiArm Edge Mopping
products.verdict: FlexiArm edge mopping at a sub-$500 price.
products.description:
The Qrevo S5V is where Roborock's edge hardware gets affordable. FlexiArm edge mopping reaches along walls and furniture, LiDAR handles mapping, and it sits in the $200 to $500 tier. It is the cheapest model here with an arm, which matters because edge coverage is the gap most budget robots never close.

It ranks fourth because it has simpler dock features than the Qrevo models above and no published suction figure. Against the Q7 M5+ below, it trades the long self-empty window for edge mopping, and for most households the cleaner baseboards are a more visible win than fewer bag changes.

Buy it if you want edge mopping on a mid-range budget and mostly clean hard floors. Skip it if you want a high-end dock with automatic features, or if suction numbers drive your decision, since none are listed.
products.idealFor: Buyers wanting edge mopping on a mid-range budget.

products.name: roborock Q7 M5+ Robot Vacuum and Mop, Up to 7-9 Weeks Self-Empty, 10000Pa
products.verdict: 10000Pa and self-empty for up to 7 to 9 weeks.
products.description:
The Q7 M5+ is the low-maintenance dock pick. It lists 10000Pa suction, LiDAR navigation and a self-empty dock rated for 7 to 9 weeks between emptying. Emptying a bin every few days is the chore that makes people give up on robot vacuums, and a dock that holds weeks of dust removes it.

It ranks fifth because its suction is roughly half the Saros, and it has no edge arm. Compared with the Q10 S5+ below, it matches the 10,000Pa suction class but adds a stated self-empty interval, which the Q10 does not list. Price is in the $200 to $500 bucket.

Buy it if you want to forget about dust bins and live in a home with mostly hard floors. Skip it if you want edge mopping, which only the Qrevo S5V and Saros list. Thick carpet will also push 10000Pa harder than the flagships.
products.idealFor: Buyers wanting minimal dock maintenance on a budget.

products.name: roborock Q10 S5+ Robot Vacuum and Mop, 10,000Pa Suction
products.verdict: A self-empty dock and LiDAR at the lowest entry price in its tier.
products.description:
The Q10 S5+ is Roborock's entry ticket. It lists 10,000Pa suction, a self-empty dock and LiDAR navigation, all in the $200 to $500 bucket. For a first robot, that mix matters more than flashy extras, since LiDAR keeps routes orderly instead of bumping around the room.

It ranks sixth because it matches the Q7 M5+ on suction but does not list a long self-empty window, which weakens its dock case. It also has no edge arm, so corners need a stick vacuum afterward. The Q7 L5 below is cheaper, but its manual bin emptying makes the Q10 a better daily tool.

Buy it as a first robot vacuum with the core Roborock features. Skip it if you want premium mopping, because the entry tier does not promise lifting or arm hardware. Carpet performance will be modest compared with the Qrevo models.

products.name: roborock Q7 L5 Robot Vacuum and Mop Combo, 8,000Pa Suction
products.verdict: The cheapest Roborock here, with 8,000Pa and a vacuum and mop combo.
products.description:
The Q7 L5 is the cheapest Roborock here and shows it. It lists 8,000Pa suction in a compact vacuum and mop combo, priced in the $100 to $200 tier. The smaller chassis suits tight apartments, and for light daily upkeep on hard floors the suction is adequate.

It finishes last because it has the lowest suction in the ranking and expects manual bin emptying. Every model above it adds a dock that handles dust for you, so ownership means a small bin you must clear by hand. That cost rises quickly in a home with pets.

Buy it for a compact apartment or a second floor where a second robot saves carrying the first one up stairs. Skip it if you want a self-empty dock, since that feature starts at the Q10 S5+. The caveat is plain: cheap hardware, more manual chores.
products.idealFor: Small apartments or a second floor.

whatMatters.detail: Pa measures suction pressure, and a higher number pulls more dirt from carpet fibers and crevices. Figures here run from 8,000Pa to 22000Pa. Find it in the title, but remember it is a manufacturer claim. Two models with similar numbers can clean differently because brush design and airflow also matter, so use Pa to sort tiers, not to split near-equal models.

A round robot cannot reach square corners, so dust collects along walls. Edge hardware solves this: the Saros 10R uses an edge cleaning arm and the Qrevo S5V uses FlexiArm edge mopping. If you have lots of baseboard and furniture edges, look for the arm name in the title or bullets, and skip the feature only if your rooms are open and uncluttered.

A self-empty dock pulls debris from the robot's bin into a bag, so you stop emptying it by hand. The Q7 M5+ lists 7 to 9 weeks between emptying, which is the clearest interval here. Check whether the listing states an interval or just says self-empty, because the two are not equivalent, and a vague claim usually hides a small bin or a short bag life.

Mop lifting raises the wet pad off the floor when the robot crosses carpet, so rugs stay dry. It matters in any home with mixed floors, and without it a vacuum and mop combo can soak a rug. The Qrevo Series lists it explicitly. Look for mop lifting or carpet detection in the bullets, and check whether the lift is stated for the whole pad or only the module.

LiDAR scans the room with a laser to build an accurate map, so the robot runs straight, efficient lines, even in dim rooms where camera-based units hesitate. Every Roborock here lists it. It helps with room-by-room cleaning and no-go zones in the app. Confirm LiDAR in the title when you compare other brands, and avoid camera-only units if your rooms are dim in the evening.

faq.a: Higher suction helps, so the Saros 10R at 22000Pa and the Qrevo S Pro at 18,500Pa are the best fits. For mixed flooring, the Qrevo Series adds mop lifting, which keeps wet pads off the carpet. The Q7 L5 will struggle on thick rugs.

faq.q: What mistake do buyers make with Roborock?
faq.a: Chasing suction while ignoring the dock and edge hardware. Those two things shape daily use more than the headline Pa. The Q7 M5+ 7 to 9 week self-empty or the Saros edge arm often matters more than 3,000 extra Pa.

faq.q: Is the Saros worth it over the Qrevo S Pro?
faq.a: Only if you want the edge arm and the extra 3,500Pa. The Qrevo S Pro is the better value for most homes, since it keeps LiDAR and premium dock features at 18,500Pa for less money.

faq.q: How do I set up a Roborock?
faq.a: Put the dock against a wall with open space around it, plug it in, then follow the app to map your home. Clear cables from the floor first. The LiDAR models, like the Qrevo S5V, build a map on the first run.

faq.q: How do I maintain the dock?
faq.a: Empty or replace the dust bag as needed and wipe the sensors. The Q7 M5+ lists 7 to 9 weeks between emptying. Clean the brush and mop pads regularly on models like the Qrevo S5V.

faq.q: Can the Q7 L5 empty itself?
faq.a: No. Per the listing data it expects manual bin emptying, so you clear the bin yourself after most runs. If you want a self-emptying dock, step up to the Q10 S5+ or Q7 M5+.

finalTake: For most buyers, the Roborock Saros 10R is the best Roborock because its edge arm and 22000Pa suction deliver the most complete clean. The Qrevo S Pro is the smarter spend if you can live without the arm. Take the Qrevo S5V for edge mopping under $500, and the Q7 M5+ if you want weeks between dust bag changes.
